clue.text: User finds equipment cut within thirty days

indicators.note: within says the trimmed kit goes inside the month

parts.note: June is a month of thirty days

indicators.note: cut says the word for equipment loses its last letter

parts.note: kit is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: Someone finds that a piece of their equipment was cut within a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'User' suggests a computer user, but here it is a drug user. 'cut' shortens KIT to KI.
explanation.definitionFit: A junkie is a drug addict, someone who uses drugs habitually; slang synonym.

clue.text: Rugby touring side initially using same pitch

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the rugby word circles the letter

parts.note: rugby union is one code of rugby

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of side

explanation.surface: A rugby side on tour starts out playing on the same pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' looks like a playing field but is musical pitch. 'using' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Singing in unison means all voices sound the same note together.

clue.text: Make plot in a frantic urge to help oneself

indicators.note: frantic suggests wild disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone hatches a plot in a frenzied wish to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging the eleven letters of MAKE PLOT IN A gives the answer. 'help oneself' here means steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Kleptomania is a compulsion to steal, a pathological urge to take things without paying.

clue.text: Former queen kept in comfort by this?

definitions.text: Former queen kept in comfort by this?

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: kept in says the queen's abbreviation sits inside the word for comfort

parts.note: cheer can mean comfort or solace

explanation.surface: A former queen is kept in comfort by the national treasury.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: royal pensions come from the public purse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the UK government department holding public funds, which pay for royal upkeep.

clue.text: Might spelling bee produce this in term?

definitions.text: Might spelling bee produce this in term?

parts.words: Might spelling bee produce this in term?
parts.note: a bee makes a humming noise, and a spelling contest yields a word; together a fashionable term

explanation.surface: Asks whether a spelling bee might produce a certain sort of term.
explanation.walkthrough: A spelling bee is a spelling contest, but read literally a bee that spells would make its noise into a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzzword is a fashionable piece of jargon, a vogue term.

clue.text: Bulging breadbasket supplied by porter?

parts.note: porter is a dark ale and breadbasket is slang for the stomach, so a swollen belly from drinking

explanation.surface: A breadbasket full to bursting delivered by a hotel porter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breadbasket' is British slang for the stomach; 'porter' is a dark beer, not a doorman.
explanation.definitionFit: A paunch caused by heavy drinking of ale, described as a belly built by beer.

clue.text: Marx's unknown work training classes in rising

parts.note: z is an unknown in algebra

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the letters are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
PE is physical education, training classes at school

explanation.surface: Marx's unknown work about training classes in an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marx' suggests Karl, but this is one of the Marx Brothers. 'in rising' turns OPPE into EPPO.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeppo was the youngest of the Marx Brothers comedy team.

clue.text: What might need endless room for casualties?

definitions.text: What might need endless room for casualties?

indicators.note: endless says the word for a hospital room loses its final letter

parts.note: a ward is a hospital room where injured people are treated

explanation.surface: Asks what would need a hospital room without limit for its injured.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: conflict fills hospital wards with casualties.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed conflict produces casualties needing hospital care.

clue.text: Angry-looking bosses to form ginger group

parts.note: red-faced means looking angry
heads are bosses or chiefs

explanation.surface: Angry bosses band together to form a pressure group.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'ginger group' is a pressure group inside a party, but here it is read literally as people with ginger hair. 'to form' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: People with ginger hair, taken together, make a group of the red-haired.

clue.text: Smart guy with passion going about bad case

indicators.note: going about means the passion word goes round the scrambled letters

parts.note: ire is passion in the sense of anger

indicators.note: bad signals the letters of case are spoilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A clever fellow gets worked up over a poor legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' could mean well dressed, but the definition is a sarcastic name for a know-all; 'bad' is the anagram signal, not a description of the case.
explanation.definitionFit: A wiseacre is a know-all, a sarcastic name for someone who thinks themselves clever.

clue.text: Send up staff to divide wages

indicators.note: to divide means the staff word splits the wages word in two

parts.note: pay is wages
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Raise the staff's share in a dispute over dividing wages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees, which fits wages, but it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up something is to mock it by imitation, a synonym for lampoon.

clue.text: Frustrate by refusing to lend cravat?

parts.note: to hog something is to keep it to yourself
a cravat is a type of tie

explanation.surface: Someone thwarts another by not letting them borrow a neckerchief.
explanation.definitionFit: To hogtie someone is to bind them hand and foot, so figuratively to hamper or frustrate.

clue.text: Chap vague about point deducted

indicators.note: about means the vague word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: grey can mean vague or ill-defined, as in a grey area
E for east is a compass point
off means taken off or deducted

explanation.surface: A man is unsure about losing a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point deducted' looks like one idea but gives two pieces, E and OFF.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey is a man's name, and crosswords use chap to clue a male name.

clue.text: Viewer suspicious about oriental girl's being topless

indicators.note: about says the suspicious word goes round the oriental letter

parts.note: fishy means suspicious
E for east, oriental

indicators.note: being topless means the girl's name loses its first letter

parts.note: Helen's is a girl's name in the possessive

explanation.surface: A suspicious onlooker is fixated on an eastern girl without a top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viewer' sounds like a person, but it is something you look through.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-angle camera lens is something through which one views.

clue.text: It isn't flat in Maidstone you finally rent

indicators.note: rent means torn apart, so these letters are pulled into a new order
finally takes the closing letter of you

explanation.surface: In Maidstone, where flats are not to be found, you end up renting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like paying for lodgings but is the past of rend, torn. Maidstone is the county town of Kent in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A slope of a mountain is steep ground, the opposite of flat land.

clue.text: Island making Welcome sign for penniless traveller?

definitions.meaning: a lake isle in Ireland made famous by a Yeats poem
read as a sign saying a hostelry costs nothing, welcome news to the broke

explanation.surface: An island puts up a welcome sign for a broke traveller.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the name into three words announcing free lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lake Isle of Innisfree is in Lough Gill, Ireland, celebrated by W.B. Yeats.

clue.text: Posh female coming in tossed out pea soup

indicators.note: coming in means these letters go inside the scrambled others
tossed signals the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: U means upper-class or posh

explanation.surface: A snobbish woman arrives and throws out the pea soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossed' rearranges OUT PEA into POTAEU; UF goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot-au-feu is a French stew of meat and vegetables, with its broth served as a soup.

clue.text: Steps beyond the suburbs?

parts.note: steps are dance moves, and beyond the suburbs lies rural land

explanation.surface: Asks what steps lie past the edge of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' suggests stairs or measures, but here it is dancing done out in rural areas.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional English folk dance, done in lines; literally a rural dance.

clue.text: Disregard second honour in decorating oneself

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the home-decorating word

parts.note: DIY, do-it-yourself, is home decorating done by yourself
OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone ignores a second honour while dressing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'decorating oneself' looks like wearing medals but means do-it-yourself home decorating.
explanation.definitionFit: To disobey is to ignore an order, so disregard is a synonym.

clue.text: Cat finding metal horseshoe in grate

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the grating word

parts.note: to jar is to grate on the nerves
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
U is horseshoe-shaped

explanation.surface: A cat discovers a metal horseshoe in the fire grate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grate' looks like a fireplace but is the verb meaning to irritate. 'finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaguar is a large spotted wild cat of the Americas.

clue.text: A girl in sort of skirt's strange bird

indicators.note: in means these letters go inside the skirt word

parts.note: a ra-ra is a short flounced skirt, with the possessive S
Vi is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl in a certain kind of skirt is an odd bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' is slang for a woman in the surface, but the answer is literal Latin for a rare bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Rara avis is Latin for rare bird, used of an unusual person or thing.

clue.text: Silver vestment's concealed zip

indicators.note: concealed says the answer lies tucked inside these words

explanation.surface: A silver vestment's hidden fastening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zip' looks like a fastener on a garment but means energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Verve is energy and enthusiasm, which zip also means.

clue.text: Move up and down area opening eyes wide

indicators.note: opening means the area letter forces its way in between the other pieces

parts.note: to eye something is to see it
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: An area that makes someone's eyes open wide.
explanation.walkthrough: A wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to go alternately up and down, like a playground plank.

clue.text: Not broadcasting rotten tune

parts.note: off means gone bad or rotten
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A dreadful tune that stops a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-air means not being transmitted, as in radio or television.

clue.text: Is Wagner epic regularly selected extract from Ring?

indicators.note: regularly selected picks letters at even intervals from these words

explanation.surface: Asks whether Wagner's epic is chosen at intervals from the Ring cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every fourth letter of IS WAGNER EPIC gives A, R, C. 'Ring' suggests Wagner's opera cycle, but it is a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc is part of a circle's circumference, a piece taken from a ring.

clue.text: Wines make a hole in cash, they say

indicators.note: they say signals the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to bore is to make a hole, and dough is slang for cash

explanation.surface: Wines that burn a hole in one's finances.
explanation.walkthrough: The sound of BORE DOUGH gives the answer; 'make a hole in cash' suggests spending heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux are red and white wines from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: Treating fraud as authentic ultimately not right in Irish county

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of

indicators.note: ultimately takes the closing letter of authentic
not says the right letter is removed from the county

parts.note: Kerry is a county in the south-west of Ireland

explanation.surface: Treating a fraud as genuine is simply wrong in an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treating' looks like a verb but is the medical sense: fraudulent treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Quackery is the practice of fake medicine, a fraud in treatment.

clue.text: Guarantee produced rap lifted from CD

indicators.note: lifted from means the letters C and D are removed

parts.note: censured means rapped, given a rap or reprimand

explanation.surface: Rap music produced and taken from a compact disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rap' looks like music on a CD but means a reprimand; C and D are removed from either end of CENSURED.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure is to make certain, a synonym for guarantee.
